controls.title: Policies, processes, procedures, and practices across the organisation
controls.description: Policies, processes, procedures, and practices across the organisation related to the mapping, measuring, and managing of AI risks are in place, transparent, and implemented effectively.

controls.title: Organisational teams committed to AI risk management
controls.description: Organisational teams are committed to a culture that considers and communicates AI risk.

controls.title: Organisational leadership takes responsibility
controls.description: Organisational leadership is responsible and accountable for decisions about risks associated with AI development and deployment.

controls.title: Risk tolerance
controls.description: Organisational teams document the risk or benefit of AI systems as part of the overall risk management process.

controls.title: Ongoing monitoring and review
controls.description: Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process and its outcomes are planned and organisational roles and responsibilities are clearly defined.

controls.title: Policies and procedures for decommissioning
controls.description: Policies and procedures are in place to decommission and phase out AI systems safely and in a manner that does not increase risks or decrease the organisation's trustworthiness.

controls.title: Roles and responsibilities established
controls.description: Roles and responsibilities and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks are documented and are clear to individuals and teams throughout the organisation.

controls.title: Teams with expertise in AI risk
controls.description: The organisation's personnel and partners receive AI risk management training to enable them to perform their duties and responsibilities consistent with related policies, procedures, and agreements.

controls.title: AI risk management in feedback mechanisms
controls.description: Organisational policies and practices are in place to foster a critical thinking and safety-first mindset in the design, development, deployment, and uses of AI systems to minimise potential negative impacts.

controls.title: Diversity and inclusion in AI teams
controls.description: Organisational teams document the AI system's intended uses, as well as user characteristics expected to interact with the AI system during the mapping and planning stages.

controls.title: Organisational risk tolerance set
controls.description: Organisational risk tolerances are communicated and documented to AI risk management teams and relevant stakeholders.

controls.title: Risk tolerances reflect legal requirements
controls.description: Organisational risk tolerances are informed by input from interested parties and reflect applicable laws, regulations, and standards.

controls.title: Policies for privacy
controls.description: Organisational policies and practices are in place to determine and address privacy risks of AI systems.

controls.title: Policies for security
controls.description: Organisational policies and practices are in place to determine and address security risks of AI systems.

controls.title: AI risk policies integrated with broader policies
controls.description: Policies and procedures apply to third-party entities, including AI producers, operators, and other components and services, within the organisation's AI ecosystem.

controls.title: Mechanisms for receiving feedback
controls.description: Contingency processes are in place to handle failures or incidents in third-party AI risks.

controls.title: Context of the AI system established
controls.description: Context is established for the AI risk assessment by documenting the AI system's intended purpose, the operator's and user's stated goals, the context of use, and any applicable laws, regulations, or standards.

controls.title: Scientific findings considered
controls.description: Scientific findings, research, and evidence are considered when identifying AI risks.

controls.title: AI risk classification
controls.description: The organisation applies risk classification methods to identify and prioritise AI risks based on potential harm and likelihood.

controls.title: Intended users and uses documented
controls.description: Specific contexts of use and foreseeable misuse are identified and documented for planning and testing of AI systems.

controls.title: Expected benefits and costs documented
controls.description: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact based on expected costs and benefits are examined by the organisation including in light of relevant context.

controls.title: Scientific principles applied to AI system design
controls.description: The scientific basis of applied AI is considered along with the organisation's risk appetite when deciding to design, develop, or deploy AI systems.

controls.title: Risks specific to AI life cycle phase identified
controls.description: Scientific methodologies to assess technical AI risks are considered and documented.

controls.title: AI data provenance documented
controls.description: AI data provenance is established for mapping and tracing potential data-related risks.

controls.title: AI system is tested
controls.description: AI system is tested for safety and bias concerns, and appropriate documentation is generated.

controls.title: Inter-dependencies documented
controls.description: Inter-dependencies and connections to and from the AI system and its component parts, including upstream data, are established.

controls.title: Risks inherited from components identified
controls.description: AI system components are categorised by whether they are in-scope for AI risk practices and by their potential contribution to risk.

controls.title: Impacts to individuals and groups are identified
controls.description: Impacts to individuals, groups, communities, organisations, and society from the AI system are identified.

controls.title: Risks and benefits evaluated
controls.description: Potential positive and negative impacts of the AI system to humans are evaluated and any benefits are weighed against costs and risks.

controls.title: Broader AI system risks identified
controls.description: Effects of AI limitations, human cognitive biases, and human fallibility are evaluated and documented.

controls.title: Practices and personnel aligned with AI governance
controls.description: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact based on exposed individuals are documented.

controls.title: AI risk and benefit magnitude documented
controls.description: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact based on impact type are documented.

controls.title: Approaches and metrics for measuring AI risk
controls.description: Approaches and metrics for measuring and evaluating AI risk, including environmental impact, are identified and documented.

controls.title: Assessments and evaluations of AI risks
controls.description: Appropriateness of AI metrics and effectiveness of existing controls are evaluated, with the results informing risk controls and risk response priorities.

controls.title: Performance of AI system evaluated
controls.description: Internal experts who did not serve as front-line developers for the AI system are involved in assessments of AI risk.

controls.title: Test sets used to measure AI risk
controls.description: Test sets, metrics, and details about the tools used during testing are documented.

controls.title: AI system evaluated for interpretability
controls.description: Evaluations involving humans are documented and analysed for potential bias or other issues.

controls.title: AI system evaluated for bias
controls.description: AI system performance or assurance criteria are measured qualitatively or quantitatively and demonstrated for conditions similar to deployment setting(s).

controls.title: AI system evaluated for security
controls.description: The AI system is evaluated for robustness and security, including adversarial testing.

controls.title: AI system evaluated for safety
controls.description: The AI system is evaluated for safety, including the potential for unintended harmful outcomes.

controls.title: AI system evaluated for privacy
controls.description: Privacy risks of AI systems, including risks from AI capabilities that could be misused for privacy invasions, are evaluated.

controls.title: Effectiveness of AI risk management evaluated
controls.description: Approaches, personnel, and documentation identified for measuring AI risk are monitored and updated, as appropriate, as the AI system evolves.

controls.title: Third-party risks evaluated
controls.description: Risk tracking approaches are considered for settings where AI risks are difficult to assess using currently available measurement techniques or where metrics are not yet available.

controls.title: Feedback is gathered
controls.description: Feedback provided by potentially impacted communities about AI risks is collected, reviewed, and considered by the organisation's AI risk management teams.

controls.title: Deployment and post-deployment risk measurement
controls.description: Measurement approaches for identifying AI risks are connected to deployment context(s) and informed by risk analysis results.

controls.title: Deployment environment monitoring
controls.description: Following deployment, runtime information is gathered and utilised by the organisation's AI risk management teams.

controls.title: AI risks based on assessments are prioritised
controls.description: AI risks and effects are prioritised based on assessments of likelihood and impact, taking into account the organisational risk tolerance.

controls.title: Treatment plans are identified
controls.description: Treatment plans are identified based on the organisation's risk tolerance, risk framework, and risk-benefit analysis.

controls.title: Response plans are in place
controls.description: Responses to the AI risks that the organisation has prioritised are developed, communicated, and planned.

controls.title: Treatment of AI risks is documented
controls.description: Treatment of identified risks includes a determination of residual risk.

controls.title: Mechanisms for sustaining risk treatments
controls.description: Mechanisms for sustaining and improving the effectiveness of risk treatments are established and documented.

controls.title: Remediation processes are in place
controls.description: Procedures for sustaining the effectiveness of AI risk treatments, including monitoring, evaluation, and updating of controls, are established and documented.

controls.title: Incidents are logged and reported
controls.description: Negative residual risks or unanticipated events are monitored and documented.

controls.title: AI risk management process is reviewed
controls.description: AI risk management processes are tested and evaluated, based on reasonably foreseeable worst-case scenarios.

controls.title: Treatment is improved
controls.description: Treatment of AI risks is improved based on assessment, performance, and feedback.

controls.title: Post-deployment monitoring occurs
controls.description: Post-deployment AI risks are monitored and incidents are captured.

controls.title: Mechanisms for AI incident reporting
controls.description: Measurable performance improvement goals for AI risk management are established, based on the organisation's goals and mission.

controls.title: Incidents are reviewed and lessons captured
controls.description: Incidents are documented and reviewed.

controls.title: AI system is updated based on risks
controls.description: Organizational teams regularly review and update the risk management approach and controls based on evidence gathered from post-deployment monitoring.
